question_text: Write the equation of continuity for fluid flow.

verification.note: Sourced from the Sri Chaitanya IPE Study Material for Jr. Students 2026-27 edition, physics volume, Chapter 10 Very Short Answer Question 6 (printed p.105). Only the question was taken; the answer, its steps and its mark split are original work — see docs/ORIGINALITY_MATHS.md. The 1+1 mark split is INVENTED and is a CLAIM until a Telangana IPE teacher confirms it. Physics hand-checked: for an incompressible fluid in steady flow, A₁v₁ = A₂v₂, so Av — the volume flux, the volume of fluid crossing a section each second — is constant along the pipe, and a narrower cross-section therefore carries a faster flow.

recall_prompt: Say the steps you would write for this answer, in order. You can speak in English, in Telugu, or in both.

page_header: Section A — Very Short Answer Question

steps.label: A₁v₁ = A₂v₂ for incompressible steady flow

where A₁, v₁ and A₂, v₂ are the
area and speed at two sections
steps.margin_note: First mark. Write A₁v₁ = A₂v₂ and name the symbols: area and speed at two sections of the pipe.
steps.why: The fluid is incompressible, so the same volume must pass every section of the pipe each second; equal Av at both sections is exactly that statement written as an equation.
common_mistakes: Writing A₁ = A₂ instead of A₁v₁ = A₂v₂ — the areas are not equal, only the product Av is.
Leaving the symbols A₁, v₁, A₂, v₂ unnamed.

recall.must_convey: That for an incompressible fluid in steady flow, A one v one equals A two v two, the area times speed at one section equal to the area times speed at another.
accept: A one v one equals A two v two
area times speed the same at every section
reject: a narrower pipe means a faster flow

steps.memory_tip: Same fluid, same pipe: A₁v₁ = A₂v₂, always.

steps.label: Av is constant: a narrower pipe flows faster
steps.mark_note: Av is constant along the pipe
lines: That is, Av is constant along the
pipe. Av is the volume of fluid
must carry a faster flow to keep
steps.margin_note: Second mark. Say Av is constant, name it as the volume flowing past a section each second, and say a narrower pipe means a faster flow.
steps.why: Naming Av as the volume flowing per second is what turns the bare equation into a statement that mass is conserved, and it is what lets a student predict that a narrower section speeds the fluid up.
common_mistakes: Never naming Av as the volume flowing per second — leaving it as an abstract product.
Saying a narrower section slows the flow, the opposite of what the equation gives.

recall.must_convey: That Av, the volume of fluid flowing past a section each second, stays constant along the pipe, so a narrower section carries a faster flow.
accept: volume flowing per second stays the same
reject: A one v one equals A two v two

steps.memory_tip: Squeeze the pipe, and the same Av forces the flow to speed up.

insider_note: Two marks: the equation A₁v₁ = A₂v₂, then that Av is constant and a narrower pipe means a faster flow. The second part is the physical reading of the equation, not just its symbols.
